display.purpose: Entry title with its own width and short-height adaptations.

headline.purpose: Take a breath; this source size is independent of text-scale.

title.purpose: Native comfort-dialog heading; responds to text-scale and the compact breakpoint.

label.purpose: Short labels beside the vital tracks.

action-entry.purpose: First visible Begin or Continue control.

settings-help.purpose: System-sans explanatory paragraphs with a 65ch measure; supplied Windows font evidence resolves Segoe UI.

settings-section.purpose: Keyboard and controller subheadings, scaled with the comfort preference.

rest-title.purpose: Wand-bench and sanctum headings; the clamped source size is independent of text-scale.

boon-title.purpose: Serif choice name, reduced to 20px at the compact breakpoint.

boon-description.purpose: Left-aligned choice description, scaled with the comfort preference.

action-descend.purpose: Filled pale-brass action beneath rest choices.

gallery-headline.purpose: Standalone system-sans page heading; compact layout changes it to 25px.

gallery-title.purpose: Named media destination above search and filters.

gallery-body.purpose: Offline utility text and destination buttons; the library does not load Cormorant.

gallery-control.purpose: Native search and select controls, independent of the game text-scale preference.

death-title.purpose: You fell; a smaller Cormorant clamp changes to 28px at the short-height breakpoint, independently of text-scale.

death-stat.purpose: Depth and carried gold in the lower report; the system-sans role responds to text-scale.

death-cause.purpose: The lower report explanation uses scaled system sans with left alignment.

action-return.purpose: Focused Return to your waystone control; its label scales with the comfort preference.

trickshot-tuning.purpose: All four native range labels and their numeric outputs share the same text-scale multiplier.

trickshot-readout.purpose: Brief clean-hit, chain, borrowed-leg and finisher cues; the fixed 13px source role sits above the action.

shadows.purpose: Text shadow supporting contextual field notes against gameplay.

shadows.name: sound-caption-text
shadows.purpose: Text shadow for the sound report below the objective.

shadows.name: flask-quantity-text
shadows.purpose: Small text shadow on runtime bottle quantities.

shadows.name: boon-taken-rule
shadows.purpose: Accepted boon uses a narrow inset brass rule rather than a floating card shadow.

shadows.name: bench-slot-inset
shadows.purpose: Inherited depth inside equipment slots; their play surface and corners are overridden while this shadow remains.

shadows.name: spell-offer-panel
shadows.purpose: Inherited shadow beneath the constrained spell-offer panel.

shadows.name: descend-enabled-hover
shadows.purpose: Inherited enabled-hover glow survives the new default shadow reset through selector specificity.

motion.name: vital-fill
motion.purpose: Play vital widths update directly; their inherited transition is removed.

motion.name: flask-fill
motion.purpose: Inherited material quantity change inside the bottle.

motion.name: toast-fade
motion.purpose: Inherited toast lifetime; reduced flashes disables this animation.

motion.name: sound-caption-lifetime
motion.purpose: One creature report remains below the objective before the HUD clears it.

motion.name: reduced-motion-duration
motion.purpose: Operating-system reduced motion overrides CSS animation and transition durations.

motion.name: boon-hover
motion.purpose: The current boon surface transition retains the inherited 2px upward hover shift; reduced motion shortens its duration.

motion.name: descend-state
motion.purpose: Inherited transition on the rest action; the operating-system reduced-motion rule overrides its duration.

motion.name: return-state
motion.purpose: The return control retains its inherited transition with a warm surface hover and no glow; reduced motion shortens its duration.

motion.name: trickshot-entry
motion.purpose: Enabled distinct-target rewards ease into slow motion through the runtime time envelope; simulation ticks retain their authored size.

motion.name: trickshot-recovery
motion.purpose: The runtime envelope returns to normal speed at the end of a rewarded window.

motion.name: trickshot-continuous-limit
motion.purpose: Maximum continuous slowdown before the runtime forces a normal-speed recovery interval.

motion.name: trickshot-recovery-interval
motion.purpose: Minimum normal-speed interval after the continuous slowdown limit.

motion.name: held-leg-swing
motion.purpose: The carried limb gathers through a harmless wind-up; elapsed ticks 6-15 sweep the solved free thigh. Committed aim and cover address the actual body contact, with durability consumed at most once per swing.

motion.name: held-leg-solver
motion.purpose: After player movement, a spring-driven wrist and constrained free thigh solve momentum and contact. Drawing interpolates those poses, including while a stationary player holds a moving limb during slow motion.

Combat experiment

Chain different enemies for a brief window of borrowed time. Take a Weaver's leg, then finish its weakened owner with it.

components.name: Combat reward readout
components.description: Inline specimen of a brief readout anchored at 16% from the top of the runtime scene. The finisher class supplies RETURNED WITH INTEREST colors; runtime shows one cue at a time and hides it on death or when disabled.
components.css: .ds-trickshot-readout { display: inline-block; padding: 6px 14px; pointer-events: none; color: #d9dfc8; background: #10232cbd; border-block: 1px solid #809d83; font: 600 13px/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-trickshot-readout[hidden] { display: none; } .ds-trickshot-readout.ds-finisher { color: #f0d096; border-color: #bd9352; }

narrative.overview:
The Living Descent is a wet, corroded alchemical refinery. Slate, mineral deposits, timber and copper carry clustered pixel detail; warm refuge light and pale living bodies establish local points of attention. Broken terrain faces, attached foliage and species-specific anatomy give the inhabited foreground its texture. Visible joints, missing limbs, bent crowns and falling vine fragments follow their physical state. Water, terrain, creatures and working machinery remain independent, mutable parts of the game. Distant refinery imagery provides atmosphere and depth.

The interface uses thin controls, warm pale lettering and quiet corners around the scene. Cormorant Garamond gives entry, room, rest and death headings their character; system text carries explanations and ordinary controls. A lower slate/brass death panel preserves the visible ivory-and-copper body. Optional Trickshot cues add native mint/brass targeting and brief combat readouts within the same scene. The separate offline capture library uses slate and brass with system-sans headings so the media remains prominent. The boot screen and authoring workshops keep their existing identity; spell-card details and shop controls retain some inherited treatments.

Source authority is [Living Descent CSS](src/styles/living-descent.css), its inherited [base CSS](src/styles/main.css), [entry markup](index.html), the [capture-library generator](scripts/screenshot-gallery.mjs), and the rendering and component sources below. The [surface brief](.impeccable/surfaces/src-game-game-ts.md) owns this expedition's composition; the [quality bar](.impeccable/quality-bar.md) and [asset manifest](docs/living-descent-asset-manifest.md) record the material direction. Generated compositions remain nonliteral references. Bounded art, Weaver/gallery and environment reviews are closed; the Trickshot/death extension has a SHIP verdict with its tuning-text and compact-panel findings resolved. Waterfall and held-limb corrections also have bounded SHIP verdicts. Source, reviewed stills and disclosed fixture measurements support this extraction within those reviews' limits. Subjective motion, listening, unaided play and hardware performance need their own evidence. [Fidelity and physical response](docs/living-descent-fidelity-and-physics.md) and [Trickshot combat](docs/trickshot-combat.md) hold implementation and validation evidence, including the separate worldgen and serial-timing gates; gameplay architecture remains in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).
keyCharacteristics: Clustered wet stone, worn copper, connected timber grain and material-rooted foliage.
Live material boundaries and detailed articulated bodies above subdued distant scenery.
Continuous anatomical attachments, visible limb loss and foliage that travels with its support.
Momentum carries water over ledges and swings a held limb's free thigh from its driven shank.
Species-specific plates, membranes, gills, scutes and state-driven faces at the established actor scale.
Serif titles paired with plain operating text.
Mostly square, lightly bordered controls, small rest-panel corner exceptions and sparse corner HUD groups.
Contextual input cues, independent flask slots and captions that follow their objective.
Optional first-contact aiming cues and a death composition that keeps the physical body visible.
A quiet capture library that discloses pose fixtures and keeps historical media findable.

rules.name: The Local Contrast Rule
rules.body: Live terrain lips, creature anatomy and actionable machinery retain readable local contrast above the distant refinery layers.

rules.name: The Title and Instruction Rule
rules.body: Cormorant carries entry, room, pause, settings, rest and death headings. Explanations and ordinary controls use their defined system-sans roles; flask keys and equipment annotations retain their source monospace treatment.

rules.name: The Live Boundary Rule
rules.body: Terrain albedo samples the real cell grid and preserves excavation and saved color overrides. Decorative refinery imagery supplies no collision or interaction; valve, refuge and pipe artwork follows real runtime anchors.

rules.name: The Attachment Rule
rules.body: Visible joints and foliage derive their anchors from authoritative anatomy, living roots or strand nodes. Severing changes the owning geometry; drawing must not restore a missing attachment.

dos: **Do** keep terrain texture and contact highlights attached to actual cells, including excavated edges.
**Do** add presentation detail within the established world-cell camera coverage and actor sizes.
**Do** keep fronds attached to living material roots and creature expression attached to simulation state.
**Do** use the same anatomical chain for Weaver drawing and limb contact, retaining visible stumps after loss.
**Do** derive held-limb drawing and damage from the solved free thigh, preserving its knee and harmless wind-up.
**Do** trace falling-water highlights along actual cell motion beneath actors and reserve pool edges for supported water.
**Do** keep vine leaves with their strand nodes through cuts and falls, and rotate grounded crowns through their spring response.
**Do** preserve the serif-title and system-text roles on the documented player surfaces.
**Do** use semantic buttons, native settings controls and the existing visible focus treatments, including the boon cards' brass focus.
**Do** keep four independently sized flask slots and place captions after the complete objective in normal flow.
**Do** retain creature anatomy and local contrast during habitat lighting and hit responses.
**Do** retain the living player's materials on solved corpse parts and keep the return panel below the visible body.
**Do** scale tuning labels and numeric values together and distinguish confirmed first contact from uncertain follow-through.
**Do** label pose fixtures, encounter clips and historical captures clearly in the library.
donts: **Don't** bake controls, labels, collision or interactive creatures into refinery imagery.
**Don't** smooth the cell-material atlas or sample across its material-quadrant boundaries.
**Don't** infer hidden-player positions in the expression renderer or advance a separate pose simulation during drawing.
**Don't** place the valve cue independently of the handwheel's runtime position.
**Don't** place hanging leaves on a fixed ceiling overlay after their supporting strand moves or is severed.
**Don't** replace the shaded creature hit response with a uniform body-filling white flash.
**Don't** treat generated studies, still-frame finish review or simulated input checks as human or hardware acceptance.
